koo.name: Koo Des (NSDOS)
paragraphs: Born in Paris in 1984, Kirikoo Des - NSDOS - is a French multidisciplinary artist, musician, performer and dancer. His work explores the intersection of movement, sound and technology.

After training at the Académie Internationale de la Danse and starting out as a hip-hop dancer in the streets of Paris, he set out to generate a “new sonic order” at the meeting point of dance, performance, live coding and electronic music. He captures living data - gestures, environmental signals, biological rhythms - through sensors and custom-built devices, notably with ORCA.

A devoted admirer of Dadaism and Lettrism, working in a DIY ethos inspired by Christian Marclay, Stelarc and Donna Haraway, he composes empirically and physically: music as a living organism. His performances and residencies span Paris, Berlin, Rome, Tokyo, Mexico City, Montréal, New Orleans, London and Amsterdam.

julien.name: Julien Thomas
julien.description: Designer, electronics designer and developer. His path spans concept cars, exobiology and musical experiments aboard the International Space Station, several years in aeronautical electronics, and robotics design for a video production studio. He now shapes the system architecture, embedded electronics and spatial interactive devices of Pigeons Studio.

history.title: How the duo took shape
history.p1: In 2020, Koo Des and Julien Thomas meet during an artistic residency organized by <matrice>Matrice</matrice> and the Institut de France. Their first shared gesture: imagining haptic devices synchronized with a virtual world, on Mozilla Hubs.
history.p2: They then keep working on these sensors through further residencies and sessions together, shaping them to their artistic world. A gyroscope, accelerometer, magnetometer, processor and screen join the device: enough to compute DFA, in the wake of <eightos>EightOS</eightos>, and to carry a visual identity strong enough that activating the object becomes a kind of ceremony.
history.p3: The haptic feedback later evolves into triphonic bone conduction. In parallel, the duo works together on digital art, synthesizers and robotics, sometimes as far as instrumenting a tattoo machine. Recently, an artistic collaboration in soft robotics has begun with Selma Lepart.

intuition.title: Intuition
intuition.description: Fieldwork around meteorological stations and biofeedback: movements of nature, turned into data, become sounds, textures and rhythms. The album completes an organic vision of music, documented in a series of five films from the field to the studio.

selm.title: S.E.L.M. - New Orleans
selm.description: A residency in New Orleans for Send Everyday Life Movement: a dance abstracted from the body, through compiled captured gestures and the “rehumanization” of data. Immersion in a performance city - second lines, Mardi Gras, Black Indians, clubs - to expand the dancer’s expressive range.

activateCities.title: Activate Cities
activateCities.description: Born from a meeting with Noam Assayag and his essay on ambulatory art. Urban journeys (Paris, Berlin, Athens, Moscow) and QR codes in public space link the album to the city: an interactive sound map to reactivate the poetic potential of overlooked places.

ecosystem.title: EightOS (∞OS)
ecosystem.subtitle: A long-term collaboration with Dmitry Paranyushkin.
paragraphs: EightOS (∞OS) is an open source operating system for the bodymind, co-created with Dmitry Paranyushkin under a CC BY-SA 4.0 licence since 2015. The project investigates natural dynamics and technologies of the self: an embodied practice, distinct from Pigeons Studio and from the AS-SIMT hardware platform.

Through physical exercises and interactive experiences, EightOS embeds its principles - adaptability, fractal variability, confluence, integrity, friction, resilience, modularity - at the level of reflexes, not just thought. Learning happens through the body: understanding a metaphor by living it.

The collaboration continues through activation programs, embodied research sessions, and SelfSense: an app and trackers that entrain fractal variability in movement, breathing and heart rate, with live feedback on the fractality of gesture.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Pigeons Studio - Koo Des (NSDOS) × Julien Thomas, creative direction, robotics and spatial sound

mission.title: Our mission
mission.content: Pigeons Studio brings together an artistic direction and a technical direction on equal footing. We design devices where gesture becomes music, movement and collective experience, for the stage, for installation and for brands. From research to deployment, we carry the project from conception to realization.

koo.title: Koo Des (NSDOS)
koo.content: A French multidisciplinary artist born in 1984 in Paris, also known as Kirikoo Des. After studying at the International Dance Academy in Paris, he set out to create the sounds on which to place his movements and to imagine an alternative sound order. Nicknamed the “techno hacker” by the French press, he distorts technological tools to link machines and matter: he collects living data using sensors on his dancing body, interactive devices and creative coding programs, then injects it into the rectilinear skeleton of techno to make an organic matrix. His work has taken him to the United Kingdom, Italy, Japan, Alaska and Indonesia, through performances, workshops and masterclasses.

julien.title: Julien Thomas
julien.content: A designer as well as an electronics designer and developer, Julien Thomas connects design, embedded systems and robotics. He has worked on concept cars, contributed to exobiology and musical experiments aboard the International Space Station, and spent several years designing and developing electronics for aeronautics. He has also worked as a robotics designer for a video production studio. At Pigeons Studio, he leads technical direction and system architecture: electronic and PCB design, embedded programming, robotic integration and spatial interactive devices. He develops the AS-SIMT hardware platform: wearable sensors combining a screen, a 9-axis motion unit and bone-conduction transducers, along with the real-time pipelines that connect sensors, sound and robots.

eightos.title: EightOS
eightos.content: EightOS (∞OS) is an open source operating system for the bodymind, co-created by Koo Des and Dmitry Paranyushkin, under a CC BY-SA 4.0 licence since 2015. The practice investigates natural dynamics and technologies of the self around principles of adaptability, fractal variability, confluence, integrity, friction, resilience and modularity, favouring direct physical experience. It extends into SelfSense, an app and trackers that entrain fractal variability in movement, breathing and heart rate. EightOS is a project distinct from Pigeons Studio and should not be confused with the AS-SIMT hardware platform.

collaborations.title: Collaborations & institutions
collaborations.content: The duo’s work has been presented at Mutek (Mexico, Montreal, Tokyo), BIAN Montreal, Gwangju Biennale, Triennale di Milano, Martin Gropius Bau in Berlin as part of the Breathe programme, IMPACT (Théâtre de Liège) and HOT‑SHOP 14 (ECCO Leather). In 2023, Koo Des was a Villa Albertine resident in New Orleans for the S.E.L.M. project (Send Everyday Life Movement), with the Matrice institute and the ETHICS lab of the Catholic University of Lille.

approach.title: Approach
approach.content: Our methodology combines research, development and artistic creation. We favor open source solutions, complete documentation and personalized support for each project.
